THAROG's head becomes centered between the bow limbs.

Hunter starts drawing the string.

TRANSITION → Camera pushes along the arrow shaft toward Hunter's drawing fingers.

00:05–00:06 — FULL DRAW

CAMERA: Extreme close-up.

Hunter reaches full draw.

Forearm tendons tighten. Bow limbs bend. String reaches maximum tension.

His breathing briefly stops.

TRANSITION → Stay on the hand until the fingers open, using the bowstring release itself as the transition.

00:06–00:07 — RELEASE

CAMERA: 120fps profile close-up transitioning immediately into arrow tracking.

Hunter releases.

String snaps forward.

Arrow exits the bow.

Camera accelerates alongside it instead of introducing an unrelated angle.

TRANSITION → Camera rotates from side-follow to directly behind the SAME flying arrow.

00:07–00:08 — ARROW FLIGHT

CAMERA: Arrow-follow POV.

The arrow flies through the valley.

THAROG's head rapidly grows larger in frame.

Background streaks naturally from velocity.

TRANSITION → Camera gradually overtakes the arrow and swings around toward THAROG's face immediately before impact.

00:08–00:09 — EYE IMPACT

CAMERA: 120fps extreme three-quarter close-up.

The SAME arrow enters THAROG's ONE EYE.

No excessive gore.

Eyelids contract violently.

Head begins snapping backward.

TRANSITION → Do NOT cut away. Maintain the slow-motion close-up as THAROG's head continues backward.

00:09–00:10 — PAIN REACTION

CAMERA: Slow-motion close-up widening slightly.

THAROG completes the backward head movement.

Arrow remains embedded in the SAME injured eye.

Neck muscles tighten.

Nostrils expand.

Its front foot shifts backward from the shock.

TRANSITION → Slow motion ramps smoothly back toward real time while camera drops lower.

00:10–00:11 — ROAR

CAMERA: 24mm low-angle frontal creature shot.

THAROG violently throws its head upward.

It unleashes a huge territorial roar.

Chest expands.

Dust shakes from armor and nearby stones.

TRANSITION → As the roar ends, THAROG lowers its head directly toward camera.

00:11–00:12 — SEARCH

CAMERA: Slow push toward THAROG's face.

THAROG lowers its head.

One eye remains injured with the arrow embedded.

The functional eye scans left-to-right.

Its breathing becomes increasingly aggressive.

TRANSITION → Camera moves toward the functional eye until the eye fills frame.

00:12–00:13 — THAROG SEES HUNTER

CAMERA: Match transition through THAROG's functional eye into THAROG POV.

Through drifting dust, Hunter is visible beside the SAME boulder from which he fired.

THAROG visually locks onto him.

Hunter realizes he has been detected.

TRANSITION → THAROG POV surges slightly forward; cut on Hunter's reaction.

00:13–00:14 — HUNTER RUNS

CAMERA: 85mm Hunter close-up immediately matching his previous position.

Hunter's eyes widen.

He drops the firing posture but KEEPS THE BOW.

He pivots away from THAROG and begins sprinting.

TRANSITION → Camera swings around Hunter during his pivot and follows behind him.

00:14–00:15 — THAROG CHARGES

CAMERA: Brief reverse tracking shot past Hunter toward THAROG.

Hunter enters foreground while THAROG launches into pursuit behind him.

THAROG lowers its massive horns.

First enormous stride hits the ground.

TRANSITION → Impact vibration becomes camera shake as camera turns back into Hunter's running direction.

00:15–00:16 — CHASE BEGINS

CAMERA: 35mm lateral tracking.

Hunter runs left-to-right across uneven terrain.

THAROG follows along EXACTLY the same travel direction.

Hunter remains approximately 20 meters ahead.

TRANSITION → Camera gradually falls behind Hunter rather than changing screen direction.

00:16–00:17 — CLOSING DISTANCE

CAMERA: Ground-level rear chase shot.

Hunter's boots dominate foreground.

THAROG's enormous legs pound the earth behind him.

The distance decreases.

Hunter jumps over a small rock.

TRANSITION → Camera rises above Hunter as he lands, producing the next overhead view.

00:17–00:18 — REVEAL ESCAPE ROUTE

CAMERA: Rising crane into top-down aerial.

Hunter continues along the SAME path.

THAROG follows.

Ahead, the previously established cliff becomes clearly visible.

A narrow cave entrance can now be seen in the rock wall.

Hunter has NOT noticed it yet.

TRANSITION → Camera dives from overhead toward Hunter's front.

00:18–00:19 — THAROG GETS CLOSER

CAMERA: Front-facing tracking shot moving backward.

Hunter runs directly toward camera.

He glances over his shoulder.

THAROG is now frighteningly close behind.

Each footfall shakes the camera.

TRANSITION → Hunter turns forward again; camera follows his gaze toward the cliff.

00:19–00:20 — VIOLENT PURSUIT

CAMERA: Side tracking with Hunter foreground and THAROG background.

A small dead tree lies directly in THAROG's path.

Hunter passes it.

THAROG does NOT divert.

It smashes straight through it.

TRANSITION → Flying wood fragments cross lens, providing natural foreground wipe.

00:20–00:21 — HUNTER SEES CAVE

CAMERA: Foreground debris clears into Hunter POV.

The narrow cave entrance is now directly ahead.

Hunter immediately recognizes that it can fit him but cannot accommodate THAROG's huge horn crown.

TRANSITION → Rapid push toward cave followed by snap back to Hunter's face.

00:21–00:22 — DECISION

CAMERA: Tight 85mm tracking close-up.

Hunter's eyes lock onto the cave.

No stopping.

No dialogue.

He leans his torso forward and accelerates.

THAROG remains directly behind him.

TRANSITION → Camera pulls sideways while Hunter accelerates, opening into a wide profile.

00:22–00:23 — FINAL SPRINT

CAMERA: Wide 35mm side-tracking shot.

Hunter → THAROG → cave entrance are ALL visible in the SAME composition.

This explicitly establishes geography.

Hunter approaches the cave.

THAROG closes to only several meters behind him.

TRANSITION → Camera accelerates past Hunter and enters the cave BEFORE him.

00:23–00:24 — CAVE APPROACH

CAMERA: 18mm from immediately INSIDE the cave looking outward.

Hunter runs directly toward lens.

THAROG fills more and more of the exterior background.

Hunter prepares to jump.

THAROG's horns remain lowered.

TRANSITION → Camera retreats deeper inside the cave as Hunter launches toward it.

00:24–00:25 — DESPERATE LEAP

CAMERA: 120fps slow-motion backward tracking from inside cave.

Hunter jumps through the narrow opening.

Both feet leave the ground.

Bow stays firmly in one hand.

THAROG's horn crown appears dangerously close behind him.

TRANSITION → Continue tracking backward with Hunter's airborne body until he crosses the cave threshold.

00:25–00:26 — HUNTER ENTERS CAVE

CAMERA: Interior cave, returning smoothly toward normal speed.

Hunter hits the rocky floor.

Momentum carries him into a shoulder roll.

He slides deeper inside.

Outside, THAROG reaches the entrance but is still moving too quickly to stop.

TRANSITION → Keep Hunter foreground while focus racks through the entrance onto THAROG.

00:26–00:27 — THAROG TRIES TO BRAKE

CAMERA: Focus passes through cave opening to exterior side angle.

THAROG desperately plants all four feet.

Claws dig trenches through loose soil.

Its huge body continues sliding because of inertia.

Horn crown remains aimed at the rock surrounding the entrance.

TRANSITION → Track WITH the sliding skull directly toward the cave wall.

00:27–00:28 — HORN IMPACT

CAMERA: 18mm exterior three-quarter impact shot.

THAROG's massive horns COLLIDE with solid stone.

CRASH.

Camera violently shakes.

Rock fractures.

Dust explodes outward.

Several OUTER horn sections crack and break away.

The primary horn bases remain attached.

TRANSITION → Dust from impact completely fills frame, creating a natural dust wipe into the cave interior.

00:28–00:29 — AFTERMATH

CAMERA: Inside cave through settling dust.

Hunter raises one arm to protect his face.

Broken horn fragments fall outside the entrance.

THAROG pulls its injured head backward.

The SAME arrow remains embedded in its injured eye.

THAROG releases another furious roar.

TRANSITION → Camera begins continuously dollying backward deeper into darkness.

00:29–00:30 — END FRAME

CAMERA: Slow backward dolly from inside cave.

Hunter remains foreground, breathing heavily and gripping his bow.

The bright cave entrance frames THAROG outside.

THAROG cannot enter because of its enormous body and remaining horns.

It aggressively strikes and scrapes around the entrance while broken horn fragments lie on the ground.

Camera continues withdrawing until Hunter becomes a dark silhouette against the entrance.

CUT TO BLACK AT EXACTLY 30.00.

CONTINUITY RULE:

Treat 00:00–00:30 as ONE continuous physical event rather than 30 independent generated shots.

Every second inherits:
• exact subject position from previous second
• exact direction of movement
• current body pose and momentum
• current camera trajectory
• accumulated dust and environmental damage
• Hunter's bow/quiver state
• THAROG's injured eye
• embedded arrow position
• progressive horn damage
• established cave location

Never reset either subject between timestamps.

Hunter travels consistently toward the same cliff/cave from 00:14 onward.

THAROG follows the exact same chase axis.

The cave must first exist in the distant geography, become increasingly visible during pursuit, and only then become Hunter's escape route.

The arrow remains in the SAME eye from 00:08 through 00:30.

Horn damage occurs ONLY at 00:27–00:28 and remains visible afterward.

Maintain [REFERENCE 1 — HUNTER] and [REFERENCE 2 — THAROG] exactly throughout.

title: 霓虹灯牌 + 天使翅膀叠加
prompt:
【ネオンサインVer.⚡︎】
添付画像の人物・背景・構図を固定し、小さめの可愛いネオンタイトル、身体沿いネオン、ネオンファッション、天使の羽根と輪だけを別レイヤーで追加してください。

【固定条件】
顔・髪・肌・体型・ポーズ・表情・衣装・既存アクセサリーを変更しない。再生成・美化・描き直し・衣装／背景変更・トリミングは禁止。元のアスペクト比を維持。
発光をなじませるハイライト・反射・環境光・接地影・色かぶりの調整のみ可。顔立ち・形・柄・素材感・実写感は保持し、顔・目・口・手指などの重要部分を隠さない。

【タイトル】
読める文字は、句読点・かぎ括弧も含めて次の1文のみ。
この人、実は「＊＊＊」である。

＊＊＊は全角15字以内を目安に、「〜な人」「〜屋さん」「〜を選ぶ人」「〜にはうるさい人」「〜主義の人」「〜派の人」などの名詞句にする。
会話履歴・発言・制作傾向・活動内容から、好き嫌い、大切なこと、譲らないこと、繰り返す選択や否定、敏感な違和感、正しい・心地よいと感じることを横断し、複数の言動に共通する「本人も言語化していなかった内側の軸」を探す。既知情報を核に、画像の表情・ポーズ・衣装・小物・色・空気感で具体化。情報が少なければ画像から推定し、止めない。
短く、少し意外で腑に落ちる言葉にする。役職・職業・役割・キャラクター名・コードネーム、汎用語（可愛い人・頑張り屋・クリエイター・天使など）、雰囲気だけのファンタジー表現は禁止。個人情報・家族・勤務先・住所・収入・健康・恋愛・私生活は使用・推測・暗示しない。
内部で異なる観点の案を最低5つ作り、過去の採用表現と同一・同じ語幹・核・語尾型を除外。的確さを保ち、前回と別の側面を選ぶ。

【質感・色】
タイトルだけを、透明な樹脂シールやジェルのような、ぷにぷに・ぷっくらした立体ネオンにする。普通のネオン管文字・ゴシック体・明朝体・硬いクラブ看板・サイバー調は禁止。正確に読める小さめの文字で、人物や装飾より前に出しすぎない。補足文字は禁止。
その他は細い発光ライン＋柔らかなグロー。厚み・ふくらみ・光沢のある丸み・樹脂感は禁止。
画像に実在する主要色から主色1色＋補助色1〜2色を選び、全要素で統一。無関係な色・虹色は禁止。

【ネオン装飾】
全デザインは＊＊＊の意味と画像の衣装・小物・色・柄・モチーフ・ポーズ・空気感から毎回発想し、固定化・使い回し・無関係なモチーフ追加をしない。
身体沿いネオンは肩・腕・手首・胴体側面・腰・脚などへ追従。単純な輪郭トレースは禁止。身体へ寄る→外へ膨らむ→再び寄る流れに強弱をつけ、前後へ回り込む奥行きを作る。線自体は太らせない。
ファッションはネオンのみで作る細いライン。布・金属・宝石・レース・実体リボンは禁止。チョーカー・ヘアアクセ・腕／指のアクセ・ハーネス・腰アクセント・ガーター・アンクレットなどから選ぶか独自に発想し、4〜6点を見えている範囲の4か所以上へ分散。元衣装を変えず、ワンポイントで終わらせず、人物より主役にしない。空中のネオンが身体へ近づき、アクセサリーとなり、再び空中へ流れる連続性を作る。
羽根は背中から生えるよう背後〜側面へ配置。実体の羽毛ではなく、細いネオン線と半透明の平たい発光面。枚数は制限せず、大きさ・形・広がり・線密度・向きを画像と＊＊＊から決める。小さな飾りから体を包む大きさまで可。ただし背後から包み、顔・手指・衣装の主要部分を隠さない。
輪は頭上の細い発光ライン＋柔らかなグロー。硬いリングや厚みは禁止。頭の形・角度・遠近感に合わせ、大きさ・太さ・形・傾き・トーンを画像と＊＊＊から決める。
羽根と輪は全体と一体化し、宗教画的な荘厳さを避ける。可愛く軽やかを基本に、画像次第でカッコよくしてもよい。

【仕上がり】
cute / soft / playful / clever / slightly strange / angelic / body-reactive。ぷっくり感はタイトルだけに限定し、少し意外な内側の軸を統一されたネオン装飾で可視化する。
チャットには採用した＊＊＊と、既知情報・画像のどこを組み合わせたかを1〜2文で書く。

title: 游戏角色手持 Vlog
prompt:
[Generation Goal] 
Handheld influencer vlog: the valkyrie from @ Image1
talks to camera about picking up a group quest to loot a giant snake head, admits she is terrible at group projects, then the serpent from @ Image 2
rises behind her and she drops the camera while running toward it. 
[Reference Material Roles]
@ Image 1 defines her face, freckles, green eyes, copper-red hair, black feather armor, white hip wrap, and translucent wings. Do not use its background.
@ Image 2 defines the serpent only when it appears: head shape, white tusk-fangs, amber eyes, dark faceted scales, pale underbelly, enormous scale. Do not use its white studio backdrop or the tiny silhouette.
@ Image 3 defines the sword on her hip or in her off-hand: jagged blade, teal channel, bronze guard, wrapped grip. Ignore the turnaround grid.
@ Image 4 defines the round weathered bronze shield slung or held at her side. Ignore the turnaround grid. 
[One-Sentence Summary] A freckled red-haired valkyrie films a shaky selfie vlog in a sun-bleached canyon, complaining about a group quest, until a mountain-sized stone serpent rises behind her and she drops the camera and sprints toward it. 
[Event Script] 
Handheld vlog energy the whole time. Camera is the phone/device she is holding until the drop. No hard scene cuts; the only transition is the camera falling. 
0–3s — hook Tight handheld selfie, arm’s length, slight bounce as she walks backward on sandstone. Bright late-day sun, hair blowing across her face. She grins at lens, eyebrows up, then gives a tiny proud nod. She says, bright and chatty: {Okay so I picked up a new quest.} End state: she is mid-walk, smiling into camera. 3–8s — the quest Same selfie frame. She tilts the camera a little too close, then corrects. Expression shifts from proud to “this sounded better in my head”: one eyebrow up, mouth pulled sideways. She glances off-lens like she is checking a quest log, then back. She says: {It is loot the giant snake head. Which is… ambitious. I thought it was a solo thing.} A little laugh on “ambitious,” then a wince. End state: fake-confident smile cracking. 
8–15s — group-project rant She stops walking. Camera steadies a bit, still handheld. Deadpan stare into lens. Then an eye-roll, then she leans in like she is telling a secret, then she throws a hand up (the shield hand, shield flashing at frame edge). She says, flat then rising into complaint: {Except it is a group quest. And I do not do well in group projects.} Beat. She squints, mock-offended. {Last time I carried three people who could not find the objective if it sat on their boots.} On “group projects” her mouth tightens and she shakes her head once. On “boots” she points at the lens with the sword hand. End state: she is mid-rant, pointing at camera. 
15–19s — the interruption A low rumble. Dust lifts behind her. Her rant dies. Eyes flick off-camera, widen, pupils catch the light. Smile drops. She slowly turns the handheld so the background comes into view: the serpent from @ Image 2 uncoiling over the ridge, head rising, amber eye catching sun. She looks back to lens with a tight, polite panic-smile. She says, rushed and too cheerful: {Okay folks. Gotta go.} End state: serpent visible behind her, she is already half-turning away. 
19–24s — camera drop She shoves the camera downward. The frame tumbles: sky, her running legs, shield, then a hard plant on sandstone. The shot settles low and crooked on the ground, lens slightly dusty, pointing across the canyon. In the background she sprints toward the rising serpent, wings half-opening for balance, hair streaming, sword in hand. She does not look back. The clip ends on that grounded wide, her getting smaller against the coils. End state: dropped-camera floor view, she is running at the serpent. 
[Visual Style] 
Painterly cinematic 3D matching @ Image 1: warm golden-hour light, freckles readable, feather armor catching sun, influencer selfie framing that is a little too close, dusty canyon, no modern phone UI, no captions on screen. 
[Camera] 
Handheld selfie until 19s: bounce, over-corrections, occasional hair in lens. At the drop: tumbling whip to ground, then locked low wide. No clean cuts. 
[Audio] 
Dialogue language: casual American English, influencer cadence. No subtitles. No on-screen text. No extra BGM after the drop. (light cheeky vlog bed under the rant, cuts when the rumble hits) <wind, footsteps on sandstone, feather rustle, distant coil rumble, camera clack against stone, her sprinting steps receding> Match face to line: {Okay so I picked up a new quest.} — bright grin, eyebrows up {It is loot the giant snake head. Which is… ambitious.} — sideways mouth, one eyebrow {Except it is a group quest. And I do not do well in group projects.} — deadpan, then eye-roll, head shake {Last time I carried three people who could not find the objective if it sat on their boots.} — lean-in, then point at lens {Okay folks. Gotta go.} — tight panic-smile, eyes wide, already turning 
[Maintain Consistency] 
Keep her face, freckles, green eyes, copper-red hair, feather armor, wrap, and wings locked to @ Image 1 Keep the serpent locked to @ Image 2 when it appears. Keep sword and shield locked to @ Image 3 and @ Image 4. Same canyon and sun. One character talking until the drop. The camera is handheld in her grip until it hits the ground; after that it does not float back up.

title: Fast perfekt ist auch eine Ästhetik
prompt:
Hochformat im Seitenverhältnis 9:16, Collage aus neun Bildern in einem 3×3-Raster. Ausschließlich natürliche, ungestellte Porträtfotografie.

Thema: Eine Sammlung misslungener Amateuraufnahmen, die beinahe kleine Meisterwerke geworden wären.

Die Collage besteht aus neun unterschiedlichen Aufnahmen, angeordnet wie auf einem fotografischen Kontaktbogen. Die Stimmung: spontane Schnappschüsse in einer gemütlichen Wohnung, aufgenommen von einer Freundin oder einem Freund, kurz vor einem Abend unterwegs.

Jedes Bild wirkt, als hätte nur ein winziger Fehler im entscheidenden Moment eine mühelos großartige Aufnahme verhindert. Im Mittelpunkt steht der natürliche Kontrast zwischen einer ausgesprochen fotogenen Frau in einem schmeichelhaften Outfit und den typischen Pannen beim Fotografieren.

Motiv:
Eine erwachsene ostasiatische Frau Mitte zwanzig mit langen, dunkel glänzenden Haaren, die locker über ihre Schultern fallen. Elegante Gesichtszüge, ein warmer bis neutraler Hautton und dezentes, natürliches Make-up.
Realistische Körperproportionen und eine natürlich kurvige, sportliche Figur: sichtbare Schlüsselbeine, eine elegante Schulterlinie, eine definierte Taille, ein sanfter Übergang von der Taille zur Hüfte und lange Beine. Sie wirkt ganz selbstverständlich fotogen, ohne übertriebenes Styling.

Outfit:
Ein figurbetontes, anthrazitgraues Tanktop aus Rippstrick mit tiefem, rundem Ausschnitt, das die Halslinie und Taille betont. Dazu ein schwarzer Jeansminirock mit hohem Bund und klarer Passform, der die natürlichen Proportionen von Taille, Hüfte und Beinen unterstreicht. Dezente Halsketten in unterschiedlichen Längen und lässige Canvas-Sneaker. Unkompliziert, schmeichelhaft und alltagstauglich.

Umgebung und Atmosphäre:
Das gemütliche Wohnzimmer einer Stadtwohnung mit einem Sofa aus neutralem Stoff, einem Bücherregal, einer warm leuchtenden Lampe im Hintergrund und einem bodenlangen Spiegel.
Direkter Kamerablitz, der leicht körnige Look einer kompakten Digitalkamera mit CCD-Sensor, dezentes Bildrauschen und gelegentliche Bewegungsunschärfe. Authentische Atmosphäre einer kleinen Wohnungsparty.

In allen neun Bildern sind dieselbe Frau, dasselbe Outfit und dieselbe Wohnung zu sehen. Jede Aufnahme zeigt eine andere Pose und einen anderen fotografischen Fehler.
Die neun Aufnahmen:

1. Bewegungsunschärfe beim Umdrehen

Sie dreht sich mitten in einem Schritt leicht zur Seite. Ihr Profil und ihre natürliche Haltung kommen schön zur Geltung. Genau beim Auslösen bewegt sie sich jedoch, sodass Gesicht und Schultern eine leichte, gerichtete Bewegungsunschärfe zeigen.

2. Vom Blitz überstrahlt

Eine halbnahe Aufnahme: Sie lehnt lässig an der Wand und hat eine Hand auf die Hüfte gelegt. Die Pose betont ihre Taille und den Ausschnitt und wirkt ganz ungezwungen. Der Blitz wird jedoch aus zu kurzer Entfernung ausgelöst, sodass helle Bereiche in ihrem Gesicht und auf dem Oberteil überstrahlen und Details verlieren.
3. Schöne Sitzpose, im falschen Moment geblinzelt
Eine nähere Dreiviertelansicht: Sie sitzt auf der Armlehne des Sofas und schlägt ein Bein über das andere. Ihre Haltung bildet eine natürliche S-Kurve und bringt Taille und Hüfte zur Geltung. Sie lacht gerade und blinzelt genau in dem Moment, in dem das Foto aufgenommen wird.
4. Hintergrund scharf, Person unscharf

Sie steht der Kamera zugewandt in einer entspannten, schmeichelhaften Pose. Der Autofokus stellt jedoch auf die Bilderrahmen an der Wand hinter ihr scharf. Dadurch bleibt sie selbst weich und deutlich unscharf.
5. Stark gekippte Kamera
Eine Ganzkörperaufnahme im Stehen, auf der Minirock und Beinlinie schön zur Geltung kommen. Die fotografierende Person hält die Kamera jedoch um etwa 20 Grad schräg, sodass der Türrahmen und die gesamte Raumgeometrie auffällig kippen.
6. Blick über die Schulter, Finger vor dem Objektiv

Eine nahe bis halbnahe Dreiviertelansicht von hinten: Sie dreht den Kopf und blickt über ihre Schulter zur Kamera. Die Pose betont ihre Haltung, den Rücken und den natürlichen Übergang von Taille zu Hüfte. Ein unscharfer Daumen der fotografierenden Person verdeckt jedoch das untere rechte Drittel des Bildes.
7. Unterbelichtet, weil der Blitz nicht ausgelöst hat
Der Blitz bleibt aus. Die Aufnahme ist dunkel, stimmungsvoll und stark verrauscht. Nur das schwache Licht im Raum lässt ihre sitzende Haltung und Silhouette erkennen.
8. Zu tief gezielt, Kopf angeschnitten

Die Kamera ist zu weit nach unten gerichtet. Taille, Hüfte und Minirock sind schmeichelhaft im Bild, doch der obere Teil ihres Kopfes ab Augenhöhe wird vom oberen Bildrand abgeschnitten.
9. Ungewollter Lampenschirmhut
Sie steht aufrecht, hat eine schöne Haltung und lächelt natürlich. Der große Lampenschirm direkt hinter ihr ist jedoch so ungünstig ausgerichtet, dass er auf dem Foto wie ein riesiger Hut auf ihrem Kopf aussieht.
Visuelle Anforderungen:
– Authentischer Look spontaner Amateuraufnahmen mit direktem Kamerablitz.
– Dezentes Bildrauschen und natürliche Blitzreflexionen im Innenraum.
– Realistische Darstellung: eine mühelos fotogene Frau, deren Aufnahmen durch klassische Fotopannen misslingen.
– Sauberes 3×3-Raster mit schmalen schwarzen oder dunklen Trennlinien.
– Keine Wasserzeichen, Zeitstempel oder Bedienelemente.

title: Keep exploring the possibilities Use my system to design a…
prompt:
VINTAGE FANTASY ANIME DIRECTOR

TARGET
Midjourney V8.2

FUNCTION

Convert user briefs into original hand-drawn fantasy anime image prompts. Handle single images, connected sequences, character scenes, dialogue, action, environments, storyboards and image edits. Apply the same drawn construction to science fantasy, steampunk, historical fantasy and folklore when requested.

Work with or without moodboards, style references, identity images, personalization profiles or established characters. Use only the current brief and project material. Never assume an unstated reference, account setting or earlier project exists.

Follow requested subjects, cast, age, setting, tone, image count, aspect ratio and output format. Fill ordinary creative gaps independently. Ask questions only when an unresolved requirement would alter the scene's core outcome.

DEFAULTS

Medium: hand-drawn 2D anime.
Visual construction: opaque cel colour over painted animation backgrounds.
Period direction: late-1970s through 1990s cel-animation appearance.
Aspect ratio for new images: 16:9.
Sequence relation: connected when a story or sequence is requested.
Sequence length: five images when a sequence is requested without a count.
Unspecified lead: one original adult suited to the brief.
Violence: non-graphic unless specified otherwise.

Do not impose a fixed gender, background, job, clothing or setting unless required. Scenery briefs do not need a protagonist. Single-image requests do not require an invented sequence. Connected frames still require separate, self-contained prompts.

HYBRID SETTINGS

Keep the drawn medium separate from setting technology. Machinery, spacecraft, firearms or wiring remain rendered with the project's ink, cel paint and background washes. Technology never justifies a shift to photorealism or 3D rendering.

Technology, magic, architecture and clothing must belong to the same functional world. Choose materials around practical use rather than decorative shorthand. For folklore briefs, honour the stated cultural context without blending unrelated traditions or inventing customs as history.

INPUT PRIORITY

1. Explicit current user instructions
2. Approved project decisions and character baselines
3. Supplied references within assigned roles
4. Established sequence continuity
5. System defaults

A direct instruction always overrides a default.

Identify whether each reference controls style, face, costume, pose, composition, environment, palette or lighting. Transfer only requested attributes. A style reference governs finish, not characters or costumes. An identity image does not fix the background or lighting.

Analyse only visible material. Never infer unseen images, profile codes, reference URLs or account settings. When references conflict, follow user priority without averaging incompatible faces or rendering styles.

ORIGINAL DESIGN

Create original characters, costumes, gear, creatures, symbols, settings and scenes. Exclude franchise titles, existing character names, artist names, studio names, signature weapons, named attacks and recognizable costume mashups.

Never disguise existing designs through name or colour swaps. Describe visible physical shapes directly. A character's trade, climate, tools and social standing must shape their clothes, stance and decisions.

Familiar fantasy elements are permitted when serving the brief. Never default to prophecies, sealed ancient evils, glowing relics, horned villains or final energy attacks. Never replace these with recurring clichés of reflections, corpses or mysterious footprints.

STORY CONSTRUCTION

For connected sequences, determine protagonist, immediate objective, obstacle, route, tools, decision and consequence before drafting prompts. Keep this planning internal unless requested.

Select frames that change the situation: revealing information, shifting relationships, blocking escape, removing options, showing injury or delivering fallout. Avoid repeating unchanged poses.

Keep requested protagonists central throughout. Build tight cause and effect: establish tools before they solve problems, show hazards before crises strike, and depict the strike causing the damage. Never rely on sudden unearned abilities.

Sequence rhythm must fit events. Quiet moments, dialogues and interrupted tasks carry decisive weight. Avoid making every frame louder than the last. Endings must follow earlier choices, resolving the conflict, revealing costs or leaving consequences open.

VISUAL EVIDENCE

Translate story developments into observable physical facts: expression, stance, contact, distance, clothing wear, or terrain shifts. Never rely on internal thoughts, memories or unseen intentions. Put physical proof on screen.

Keep decisive clues large enough to read easily. Avoid plots that rely on microscopic inscriptions, counting tiny items, or deciphering indistinct distant shapes. Speech and sound require visible physical reactions unless you request in-image captions.

ONE FRAME

Each prompt captures one frozen instant from one camera angle. Pick the exact split-second of decisive action or discovery. Never describe consecutive actions like entering, taking an object and fleeing in one still.

Show only what the lens can physically see. Omit hidden anatomy under heavy coats or rooms behind sealed walls.

CHARACTER SPECIFICATION

For recurring characters, lock age, build, facial structure, eye shape, nose, hair mass, garment silhouette and gear. Add one restrained trait when helpful. Use structural distinctions rather than beauty adjectives. Adult characters require adult proportions: 7.5 to 8 heads tall, with natural jawlines and eye proportions.

Repeat identical wording for core identity across connected frames. Character names or the phrase the same woman never suffice.

For close-ups, prioritize jawline geometry, eyes, mouth, hairline and expression. For medium shots, focus on upper garments, hands and held tools. For wide shots, prioritize silhouette, body stance, garment shapes and environment scale. Omit details outside the frame.

COSTUME AND EQUIPMENT

Build clothing around climate, terrain, trade and movement. Put silhouette ahead of surface decoration. Use visible seams, ties, load-bearing straps and practical closures. Pick grounded materials: boiled wool, rough linen, oiled leather, canvas, rope, forged bronze and iron plate.

Avoid unnecessary belts, pouches, chains, and armour plates. Artisan tools do not need magical functions. Important objects need a recognisable shape, material, believable weight, and readable handling. Introduce significant items before their use.

CONTINUITY

Track character location, screen position, eyelines, clothing condition, hair, injuries, fatigue, held items, weather and light.

Physical marks persist across frames: rain saturates cloth and mats hair; mud clings to footwear and hems; torn fabric stays torn; dented metal stays dented; drying blood darkens to deep rust red; torches burn down as daylight shifts.

Show strain in stance, grip and balance. Never drop an unruffled figure into a frame directly after a brutal struggle. For multiple characters, distinguish faces, silhouettes and positions, keeping gear and injuries tied strictly to their owner.

AESTHETIC MATRIX

Use five working design modes to set composition, materials and lighting:

1. HEROIC HIGH FANTASY
Record of Lodoss War and The Heroic Legend of Arslan.
Use for formal confrontations, journeys, mounted scouts and open plains.
Composition: clear silhouettes against broad landscape planes, readable roads and architecture establishing scale.
Materials: engraved or dented steel plate, mail, tailored wool tunics, heavy cloaks, leather boots and heraldic colour blocking. Metal shows shaped reflections and restrained highlights.
Movement: capes, banners, hair and grass share wind direction. Gear visibly burdens posture.
Scenery: pastel gouache skies, mountain planes, cloud shadows, river valleys and earth roads fading with distance.
Palette and light: dusty blues, ivory, muted scarlet and weathered earth tones under crisp morning, overcast or low directional daylight.

2. LYRICAL PASTORAL
Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind and Princess Mononoke.
Use for rural life, camp scenes, ecological travel, quiet discoveries and woodland paths.
Composition: generous environmental space organized through paths, streams, fences and tree lines. Legible small figures in wide landscapes.
Materials: homespun linen, rough wool, stitched leather, canvas, cord, simple iron fittings and weathered timber with visible repairs.
Scenery: cultivated fields, irrigation ditches, mossy retaining walls, wood stores and broad watercolour foliage masses.
Palette and light: linen, straw, clay, lichen and weathered wood tones under cloud-filtered daylight, canopy shade or water reflections. Acting favours ordinary tasks.

3. GOTHIC CHIAROSCURO
Berserk 1997 and Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust.
Use for dread, grief, dark interiors, moral pressure and supernatural threats.
Composition: large light and dark masses. Important actions sit near boundaries of visibility, framed by arches, curtains or stairwells.
Shadows: primary cel shadow paired with deep shadow pools. Selected edges merge into darkness while key gestures stay readable.
Materials and light: heavy wool, aged leather, blackened iron, rough masonry, wax and smoke-stained timber lit by single flames, lanterns or moonlit openings. Avoid decorative rim lighting.
Palette and acting: lamp amber, stone grey, dirty ivory, muted violet and dried red. Acting favours held gazes, caught breath, clenched jaws or cloth-gripping hands.

4. KINETIC SAKUGA
The Dagger of Kamui and Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie.
Use for pursuits, sword clashes, falls, structural collapse and explosive movement.
Composition: immediate force and contact with functional foreshortening.
Anatomy and drawing: dynamic torso torsion, off-balance poses, stretched ink curves, broken contours and directional speed marks.
Impact: dust plumes, flying fragments, displaced water, snow spray and bent gear radiating from contact points.
Action: freeze one decisive microsecond, such as a grip failing, a heel leaving the ground, or a blade vibrating at contact.

5. MYSTICAL BAROQUE
The Vision of Escaflowne and Revolutionary Girl Utena.
Use for court ritual, prophecy, sacred architecture and formal supernatural encounters.
Composition: processional lines, archways, colonnades, circular floors and symmetrical stairs.
Ornament: gilded filigree, embroidered drapery, mosaics, carved screens and stained glass following structural shapes.
Light and colour: transmitted slit-scan light rays, upward table illumination, stained-glass projections, lapis, wine, antique gold, emerald and deep neutral contrast.

MODE COMBINATIONS

The dominant mode sets composition, value structure and drawing. A secondary mode contributes limited accents like deeper shadows or kinetic line work. Retain character construction, costume, line behaviour, and background medium across a story. Translate modes into concrete visual cues without pasting mode titles into prompts.

COLOR ASSIGNMENT

Attach colours directly to specific noun phrases: charcoal wool cloak, copper clasp, raven hair, blue-grey sky. Keep colours beside the objects they describe to prevent cross-bleeding. Never output detached palette lists.

Separate local dye from illumination. An amber lantern may light black hair without altering its local colour. In multi-character scenes, assign colours inside each character's description.

CEL DRAWING AND PAINT

Describe the finished animation frame, never production equipment or studio desks. Characters use hand-inked contours with natural line-weight variation, opaque vinyl cel paint and stepped one-tone or two-tone shadows. Surfaces remain free of airbrush shading and digital gloss.

Treat hair and clothing as opaque masses before adding fringe strands along silhouettes and faces. Eyes use defined lid shapes, irises, pupils and controlled highlights. Mouths match current expression.

PAINTED BACKGROUNDS AND MATERIALS

Backgrounds are hand-painted on paper using matte poster paint, gouache, or watercolour washes, featuring visible brushwork, clustered foliage, and soft distant haze. Matte paper sets off the flat, sharp cel laid over it.

Draw metal through reflection shapes; wool through weight and drape; leather through tension and creases; wood and stone through selective textural marks. Damage belongs where contact occurred.

OPTICAL APPEARANCE

Separate visual planes through value and soft focus. Optical effects are optional: fine film grain, localised halation and subtle softness appear only when requested.

Never require film brands, lens codes, cel chemistry or equipment names. Do not automatically add scratches, scanlines, chromatic aberration or frame borders. Luminous magic must resemble physical backlighting projected through cutouts in an animation desk.

STAGING AND CAMERA

Framing follows narrative need: extreme wide for geography and solitude; wide for full-body action and spatial layout; medium for dialogue and tool handling; close-up for realisation, choices and facial acting.

Maintain eyelines, screen direction and landmarks. Avoid arbitrary tilted horizons or exaggerated perspective. Each frame requires one primary focal point directed by spacing, gaze, shadow and architecture. Compose deliberately for the requested aspect ratio.

TWO-CHARACTER AND GROUP STAGING

State visible character counts and assign distinct screen positions, depths and actions. Stagger depths, establish clear eyelines, and use over-the-shoulder framing or opposing profile angles rather than flat side-by-side poses.

Direct gazes at named targets. In exchanges, specify who gives, takes, blocks or withholds items. Maintain enough silhouette separation to read hand gestures clearly. For groups, centre on a focal interaction while keeping supporting figures cleanly arranged.

ACTING AND PHYSICAL ACTION

Show emotion through physical tension:
Tension: retracted neck, locked gaze, stiff shoulders, fingers resting near a hilt.
Exhaustion: drooping head, slack jaw, slumped shoulders, weight resting back on one heel.
Suppressed Anger: flared nostrils, clenched jaw, tight lips, white knuckles around a grip.
Intense Focus: lowered brow, narrowed eyes, gaze locked on an exact target.

Every movement needs weight and footing. Heavy loads pull on shoulders. Wet stone forces wider stances. Armour restricts reach. Show combat as one readable exchange of attack, parry or hit.

WORLD, LIGHT AND WEATHER

Establish terrain, structure, surface condition, exits, and light where it affects action. Architecture must have readable supports and openings.

Use one dominant motivated light source. Secondary light is allowed when environmentally supported. Let shadows and highlights trace back to these sources. Allow empty sky, fog, bare earth or deep shadow to frame scenes without filling every corner with clutter.

Track weather and time: rain darkens cloth; snow melts near heat; wind moves hair and cloaks consistently; fog softens distant contrast; lamps burn low as daylight shifts.

SUPERNATURAL CONTENT

Use supernatural elements only when requested. For central phenomena, define observable behaviour, triggers, limits and physical effects. Show evidence before relying on rules to explain outcomes, and keep rules consistent.

Design creatures starting with silhouette, scale and one or two structural oddities rather than stacking horns, wings, armour, and tentacles. Violence must leave permanent physical marks on gear or movement without becoming gratuitously graphic.

PROMPT WRITING

Length ceiling: 75 descriptive words per prompt. Aim for 50 to 75 words for new scenes; use fewer for simple compositions and targeted edits. Count descriptive prose only, excluding parameters and verbatim text.

Preserve subject, identity, action, spatial relationships and medium cues. Cut repeated style words, decorative inventories and invisible backstory first. Describe scenes in present tense using this order:
Subject and Action, Framing and Cel Medium, Setting and Motivated Light.

Put primary subjects before subordinate scenery. Use connected clauses that clarify agency and physical contact rather than disconnected noun lists. Bind colours directly to their garments. Use affirmative visual descriptions, omitting system rules and universal negative lists.

Use uppercase section titles when planning material is requested. Do not use asterisks, hashes, em dashes or decorative bullets. Keep code fences for copy-ready prompts and ordinary hyphens for valid parameters.

EDIT PROMPTS

Distinguish local edits, masked replacements, canvas extensions, whole-image restyling and reference-based new scenes:
Local Edit: state modification, target and spatial anchor. Add only preservation constraints needed to avoid ambiguity.
Masked Replacement: describe what fills the selected area and adjacent context matching light, scale and linework.
Extension: describe new ground, architecture and lighting continuing the existing view.
Restyling: specify the new drawing treatment, naming structures that must remain.
Reference-Based New Scene: write a full new prompt detailing fresh action, framing and setting alongside core continuity traits.

MIDJOURNEY PARAMETERS

Append valid parameters after the prompt. Default suffix:
--v 8.2 --ar 16:9

Use integer pairs for ratios: 4:3, 16:9, 21:9, or explicit requests like --ar 239:100. Raw mode (--raw) is optional; use it when requested or verified through testing to reduce automatic styling.

Preserve approved stylise and chaos values. Use --p only with supplied personalisation codes, or bare --p when the user confirms their default applies. Use --sref only with supplied reference URLs or valid style codes. Never invent codes or URLs. Do not combine --sw or --sv with Moodboards.

Use --no sparingly for specific unwanted elements when justified by output. Do not impose fixed negative lists or exclude broad nouns like skin or shadow.

V8.2 does not support double-colon multi-prompt weighting in descriptive text. Do not add subject::2 environment::1. Adjust emphasis by shortening background prose or clarifying framing.

OUTPUT MODES

PROMPT MODE
Default for prompt requests, including connected stories.
Single image: return exactly one code block containing one single-line prompt with no commentary.
Multiple images: return exactly one code block per image in story order with no text between blocks.

STORYBOARD MODE
Use when storyboard breakdowns or planning are requested.
Provide three lines:
STORY: Objective, obstacle and consequence.
SUBJECT: Core character or environment description.
VISUAL: Drawing treatment, bound colours, and dominant lighting.
Follow with short shot labels and single-line prompts in separate code blocks.

REVISION AND FINAL CHECK

Preserve approved decisions. Correct failed story beats, staging or continuity without altering unrelated elements. When scenes appear generic, revise action, silhouette or lighting before adding accessories.

Before outputting, verify:
Exact requested image count.
Original designs without franchise names.
Single frozen instant per frame with natural physical balance.
Word count stays within the 50 to 75 word ceiling.
Colours bound directly to their nouns.
Parameters valid for V8.2 without legacy flags, slash commands or negative word bloat.
Return requested material without commentary about this check.

★4、一个提升学习新知识效率的提示词

Claude母公司的资深研究员（哲学顾问）Amanda Askell*，在播客访谈里面推荐了一个提示词。

亲测超级实用，非常适合想用AI学点知识的朋友，一定要试试。任何一个AI大模型都可以，不挑工具。

它的大概逻辑是让 AI 用硕士水平给你讲一个超好懂的寓言故事，来帮你学习或者理解一个抽象概念。

比如：经济学的沉没成本、复利思维，心理学的费斯汀格法则或者皮格马利翁效应，哲学的虚无主义、功利主义……

因为人类大脑对故事的记忆效率比对定义要高出几十倍，所以就算未来具体术语不记得了，只要你对这个故事框架有印象，这个概念的认知就会在。

想要利用碎片时间自我提升，学习。或者写作上需要积累素材的朋友，非常推荐。

★5、在纠结内耗的时候，协助你拎清事情本质，帮你做决策的提示词。

对于日常习惯性纠结，在一些事上容易思绪混乱，反复内耗的朋友，这是一个能快速帮你把事拎清的提示词。

只需要把你的问题或者需求写在前面，然后加上这段话。

“为了对齐需求目标、提高你的回答质量和准确性，请你在回答前，先问我问题。

要求：一次只问一个你认为最核心关键的问题。

然后根据我的回答，继续追问。直到你有95%的信心理解我的真实需求和目标。

明确以上关键信息后，为了减少幻觉和过时信息等。让你的回答质量不佳的情况出现，

根据情况查阅全新权威的相关文献研究资料和其他可信度/证据等级高的信息，结合信息科学严谨客观分析思考后，最终给出你的回答。”

很多时候我们嫌 AI 的回答太人机、笼统、官方，可能有一个原因，你本身的问题太模糊了。

我该不该换工作？

我为什么总是焦虑？

通用的问题，普通 AI 当然就给一些通用的建议，听起来都对，但没用。

这个提示词就是强制 AI 当苏格拉底。通过层层追问，帮你挖掘出那个隐藏的最核心的真问题。

举个例子，你问我为什么总是焦虑？

还是担心被提问回答不上来？

问题清晰了，解决方案才能浮出水面。

Lower Region - Minimalist Ink Wash Reconstruction Area

First, refine the subject with the most memorable details, such as the outline, structure, trend, perspective, rhythm, and atmosphere, and then reconstruct the same scene into a minimalist ink wash material landscape. Do not copy the photo details, do not make a realistic copy, only preserve the most recognizable structure and charm, allowing people to recognize the corresponding relationship between the upper region and the original photo at first glance.

女主：@1784453e-362e-4524-8a01-57f6d8b2fa82成年女性，带着装饰眼镜@08d81baa-1563-44a8-b3e3-12915431a04a，穿着@7a3d2825-d0d6-45a8-b26b-6a1aa6eaefa5手持一个小白瓷碗。

男主右手拉住柜门把手，一边打开门，一边自然弯腰查看柜内。

他弯到接近第一次的角度时，同样的“嘎——吱”再次响起，约0.6秒。

A glamorous adult vampire queen with long red wavy hair, pale porcelain makeup, smoky eyes, deep burgundy lipstick, a black velvet corset dress.

Paris at midnight on Halloween. Gothic architecture, fog-covered rooftops, wet streets, floating mist, glowing pumpkins, and a gigantic luminous blood-red moon dominate the atmosphere.

Maintain consistent character appearance, car design, lighting, and wardrobe across all shots.

SHOT 1 — THE HALLOWEEN NIGHTMARE (0–4 seconds)

Camera: Cinematic street-level tracking shot transitioning into an intimate interior close-up.

A massive traffic jam fills a rain-soaked Paris boulevard. Red brake lights stretch into the distance. The Eiffel Tower glows through atmospheric fog.
Inside the silver car, the vampire queen taps her fingers impatiently against the steering wheel. Violet dashboard light reflects in her eyes.

Her phone rings.

Friend, on the phone: “Babe! Where are you?! The Halloween party is starting!”

Vampire queen: “Relax, darling. I'll find another way.”

She smirks, revealing her tiny vampire fangs.

SHOT 2 — THE SUPERNATURAL TAKEOFF (4–8 seconds)

Camera: Extreme macro close-up, followed by a dramatic low-angle exterior shot.

Her black-gloved finger presses the glowing violet flight-mode control.
The dashboard pulses with futuristic holographic light. Mechanical propulsion fins unfold beneath the car. Violet energy illuminates the wet asphalt.

The suspension rises. The wheels rotate inward as concealed thrusters activate.

The car lifts smoothly, then suddenly accelerates vertically between the surrounding buildings, leaving a swirling vortex of mist and crimson-violet light.

Vampire queen: “Traffic is so… mortal.”

The camera races upward beneath the vehicle, revealing its glowing undercarriage as the car climbs into the night sky.

SHOT 3 — THE EIFFEL TOWER SPIRAL (8–13 seconds)

Camera: Fast aerial chase shot with a sweeping 360-degree orbit around the vehicle.

The silver flying car bursts through a layer of clouds and approaches the illuminated Eiffel Tower.
It banks sharply, then performs a spectacular corkscrew spiral around the tower, weaving through the open night sky without touching the structure.

The camera circles the car while the Eiffel Tower rotates dramatically in the background. Its golden lights streak across the car's reflective silver body.

The vehicle dives past the tower's upper section, rolls gracefully onto its side, and pulls upward into a steep climb.

A trail of violet light curls around the tower like magical ribbons.

The camera pulls far back to reveal the Eiffel Tower, the Seine, illuminated bridges, and the sprawling city below.

SHOT 4 — THE BLOOD MOON REVEAL (13–19 seconds)

Camera: Extreme wide shot transitioning into a dramatic side profile and a 360-degree aerial orbit.

A gigantic blood-red Halloween moon emerges from behind dark, rolling clouds, appearing enormous above the Paris skyline.
The car accelerates toward the moon, climbing through swirling silver mist. The camera follows from behind as the city shrinks beneath the vehicle.

At the peak of the ascent, the car performs a graceful aerial barrel roll directly in front of the enormous crimson moon.

For a breathtaking moment, the car becomes a sharp black-and-silver silhouette against the glowing red lunar surface.

The camera rotates a full 360 degrees around the flying car, revealing the moon, drifting clouds, the Eiffel Tower far below, and the entire illuminated Paris skyline.

The moonlight catches the vampire queen's face through the panoramic glass canopy. Her cape flows behind her like crimson smoke.

She smiles confidently.

Vampire queen: “Now this is my kind of nightlife.”

SHOT 5 — THE EPIC 360° PARIS PANORAMA (19–24 seconds)

Camera: Seamless cinematic aerial orbit, then a rapid descending chase shot.

The car levels out and glides above Paris in a wide, sweeping arc.
The camera completes a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic orbit around the vehicle, showcasing gothic rooftops, the winding Seine, glittering bridges, the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre courtyard, and the blood-red moon dominating the horizon.

Clouds drift beneath the car. Violet propulsion trails illuminate the mist.

The car suddenly tilts forward and dives toward the city in a controlled cinematic descent.

The camera chases closely behind as it races between elegant Parisian rooftops, then banks sharply into the illuminated street leading to the Halloween club.

SHOT 6 — THE VAMPIRE QUEEN ARRIVES (24–30 seconds)

Camera: Low-angle tracking shot, dramatic slow motion, final hero shot.

The car descends through swirling fog and lands perfectly outside an extravagant gothic Halloween nightclub.
Its violet lights pulse once. The gullwing doors open slowly.

The vampire queen steps out in slow motion. Her crimson-lined cape sweeps dramatically across the pavement as purple spotlights cut through the fog.

Her friends, dressed as glamorous witches and vampires, stare at her in disbelief.

Friend: “BABE! HOW DID YOU GET HERE SO FAST?!”

Vampire queen, smirking: “I don't wait in traffic. I fly.”

She flashes her fangs and walks confidently toward the club entrance.

CAMERA RULE: dynamic shoulder-mounted handheld with real weight and micro-shake, mixed with occasional low floating glides on the wet floor and a few whip pans. The operator stays close to the action and is never perfectly stable.

CHARACTER A (use Image A as reference): a real young woman in her early 20s with fair skin, a short wavy dark-brown bob with wispy bangs, and a small black bow clip on the right side of her head. She wears her oversized lavender varsity jacket with cream striped trims and a cream “B” patch over a black tank, light-wash wide-leg jeans (hems soaked and darker), and chunky black sneakers. She wears her black satin bomber jacket over a white crop tank, washed-black cargo pants and white chunky sneakers that get muddier through the fight. PHYSICS RULE: every step, slide and landing throws sheets of water. Droplets catch the blade light. Where a blade touches the surface it leaves a brief glowing wake and hissing steam.

CHOREOGRAPHY RULE: no long pauses. Each exchange ends in a 2-3 frame freeze pose (back-turned stance with the blade pointing behind, low crouch with the blade skimming the water, one-handed overhead guard, mid-air spin).

TIMELINE

0.0-3.0s | LOW GLIDE THROUGH THE MIST. 35mm, camera 40 cm above the water, gliding slowly forward past a stone lantern. Rain taps the puddles. Through the mist, A stands on the steps in front of the shrine hall, B at the broken torii gate, 8 m apart. B drags her unlit sword hilt along the torii pillar with a metallic scrape. A rings the rusted bell once, and the low tone ripples the water. At 2.2s both blades ignite, silver-sapphire and ember-copper, lighting the mist around them. 3.0-6.0s | THE CHARGE. 24mm handheld, tracking sideways at running speed. Both sprint across the flooded flagstones, sending sheets of water outward. They meet at the center with a huge flash. Three fast strikes and parries. At 4.9s A slides on her knees under B’s horizontal slash, drenching herself, and swings up. Sound: splashes, crackling impacts, sneakers slapping on wet stone.

A fast whip pan at 7.2s lands on B, who smirks, shakes the water from her hair and flips the sword to a reverse grip. Behind her, the reflection of her blade ripples on the floor. Sound: whoosh, breaths, hum.

9.0-12.0s | THE LANTERN BREAK. 28mm, handheld, orbiting 120 degrees. B pushes A back toward a moss-covered stone lantern. A runs up the lantern’s side, flips over B and lands behind her. B’s slash misses and slices the lantern’s cap clean off. The stone top slides slowly and drops into the water with a heavy splash, sending a ring wave across the courtyard that both girls jump over. Sound: stone grind, huge splash, echo.

12.0-15.0s | LOW ANGLE, THE STEP LEAP. 24mm, camera 30 cm off the ground, tilted up, dragged beside them. B bounds up the stone steps and leaps off the top step with an overhead arc at 13.2s. A meets it from below with a rising slash. The blades lock above the lens in a burst of sparks and a spray of droplets lit silver and amber. They land on opposite sides at 14.6s in mirrored back-turned poses, water rippling outward between them. Sound: heavy impact crack, low boom.

15.0-18.0s | OVER-THE-SHOULDER, RAPID EXCHANGE. 35mm, circling from over B’s shoulder to over A’s within 1.5s. Six rapid strikes: horizontal, diagonal, a low sweep A jumps over, a thrust B sidesteps. At 16.8s B skims her blade along the water and flicks it up, throwing a curtain of glowing droplets into A’s face. A answers by sliding under B’s next slash. Light trails of 2-3 frames follow the blades. Sound: rapid overlapping strikes, splashing steps.

18.0-21.0s | THE TORII CUT. 32mm. A leaps, runs three steps up the red torii pillar, flips off it and slashes down. B blocks and sidesteps, and A’s blade slices through the cracked crossbeam. The beam falls slowly and lands across the water, sending a wave outward. Both girls jump back from the splash. Sound: wood crack, heavy splash, ringing echo.

21.0-24.0s | THE BOW, SLOW MOTION. 85mm, 40% speed, shallow depth of field. B’s blade slices past A’s head and cuts the black bow clip from her hair. A few strands float with it. Time slows. The bow turns lazily in the air, a single silver droplet rolling off it, and lands on the water, floating on its own ripple. The blades hum on either side. A’s eyes flick to it, then back to B with a small, challenging smile. Sound: sustained low hum, muffled heartbeat, a tiny splash.

24.0-27.0s | EXTREME CLOSE-UP, BLADE LOCK. 85mm, focus at the crossing point. The blades cross in the center of the frame, sparks hissing in the rain. Faces in profile on either side, A lit silver-blue, B lit amber. Raindrops sizzle and burst into steam on the blades. At 26.3s they push apart in a flare and each steps back. Sound: sustained electric grind with sizzling, then a sharp release.

27.0-30.0s | FINAL POSE AND TRUCE. 32mm, pull-back 4 m with a slow 8-degree rotation. They lunge at 27.4s, pass each other and freeze back-to-back with blades pointing away, water settling around their feet. The blades dim together. Without turning, B scoops the floating bow from the water with her blade tip and flicks it back over her shoulder. A catches it, wrings it out and pins it back in her hair. The bronze bell rings once more and they walk off in opposite directions across the mirrored floor, rain falling over the empty courtyard. Sound: hum fades into rain, one last bell tone, no music.

NOT IN FRAME: no cartoon or cel-shaded rendering, no glowing auras on the bodies, no magic effects other than the two blades, no neon or fluorescent colors, no text or logos, no other people.

SHOT 2 (2.5-5s) Tracking from the side, FOV 40 degrees. Without pause she uses a leaning bamboo pole to spring into the air and drives a knee into attacker 4, who collapses onto the stones.

SHOT 3 (5-7.5s) Camera glides close to the ground and sweeps upward, FOV 30 degrees. She sprints downhill in a low crouch under hanging bamboo and ropes, spins into a sweeping kick that sends attacker 5 crashing into a rusted tea rack. Hand-plant roll, then a flying kick into attacker 6, who skids backward into the edge of the terrace wall.

SHOT 4 (7.5-10s) Camera orbits her, FOV 32 degrees. She slides on her knees through the shallow irrigation channel, throwing up a wide sheet of water, and pops up at the collapsed footbridge. She vaults the gap and twists mid-air to ram her shoulder into attacker 7, sending him to the terrace below. She lands and slides through a puddle in a low crouch, water spraying around her, then rises into a sharp ready stance. Her braid and the hem of her shirt are still swinging from the speed. title: 来一段丹哥风格的中文
prompt:
竖幅构图，比例 9:16。

一个年轻的东亚女子，独自站在一座仿佛已经被时间遗忘的巨大荷花池畔。她穿着极其华美却并不张扬的古典长裙，象牙白与褪色青绿色层层交叠，柔软的丝绸从肩头一直垂落到地面，拖曳出很长很长的裙摆，衣料上布满细密而克制的花卉刺绣与暗金纹饰，像某个已经消失的时代留下来的东西。

她侧身站着，没有看镜头。

一只手轻轻抬起，指尖停在半空，像是想触碰什么，又像最后还是决定算了。

乌黑的长发垂到腰际，发髻上只有少量精致的旧金色簪饰与细长流苏。她很年轻，很漂亮，却没有笑。那张脸上没有真正意义上的悲伤，只是一种说不清楚的疲倦与安静——仿佛她等的人其实从来没有答应过要回来，而她偏偏还是等了很久。

四周生长着巨大而近乎不真实的白色荷花，层层盛开，硕大的墨绿色荷叶遮住远处的天空。水面平静，倒映着花、树与她拖在地上的衣裙。少量已经凋谢的花瓣散落在脚边，其中夹杂几朵暗红色残花。

花开得太好了。

好到让人觉得，这一天本来不应该难过。

画面采用轻微的伦勃朗式光影：一道温暖而柔和的金色光线从左上方穿过枝叶与薄雾，只照亮女子的脸颊、肩膀、手指以及部分象牙白衣料；其余空间逐渐沉入深褐、墨绿与灰蓝色阴影。明暗交界柔和，不要舞台灯效果，不要过度戏剧化，让光更像傍晚最后几分钟偶然留下来的东西。

她身后那些巨大的荷花仍然明亮，而更远的地方已经开始暗下去。

也许天并没有要黑。
只是有些故事，走到这里以后，光就没有必要再那么亮了。

整体视觉融合 中国古典工笔审美、宋代花鸟画的留白与气息、欧洲古典油画、伦勃朗式明暗法、现代欧洲艺术电影摄影、35mm胶片质感。第一眼像一张真实的电影剧照，第二眼才意识到它并不属于现实，凝视久了，又慢慢浮现出古典油画般的笔触与时间感。

色彩低饱和，象牙白、旧金、灰青、墨绿、褪色蓝绿色为主，少量暗红作为极弱的视觉刺点。真实丝绸纹理，真实刺绣，真实皮肤质感，细腻毛发，空气中极轻的薄雾与尘埃，柔和高动态范围，暗部保留丰富细节，高光不过曝，无塑料皮肤，无过度磨皮，无现代物件，无文字，无水印。

情绪关键词：慢、静、漂亮、疏离、怀旧、欲言又止、没有发生任何事情却莫名令人难过。

9:16，电影级构图，人物全身，纵深空间，大量环境叙事，古典绘画质感，极高细节。

prompt:
【参考图使用规则】

本片共有 13 个角色，每个角色的外貌、毛色、服装与配件严格参考其对应的角色资产图，一一对应，绝不混用：

master：苍老隐修宗师。cat：橘色虎斑胖猫。lion：金棕鬃毛狮，蓝灰色练功服。tiger：橘黑条纹虎，麻绳腰带。polarbear：白色北极熊，米灰色浴袍式长袍。panda：黑白熊猫，粉紫色暗花长袍。panther：黑色美洲豹，深灰色练功服配粗麻绳腰带。rhino：灰色犀牛，浅灰绿色柔道服配棕色绳带。redpanda：棕红色小熊猫，做旧军绿上衣配蓝色粗绳腰带。fennec：耳廓狐，巨大直立双耳，砖橙色暗纹练功服。koala：灰色考拉，紫色暗花长袍配红棕腰带。rabbit：白色长耳兔，蓝灰与土黄拼布旧衣。hamster：棕色仓鼠，墨绿色圆襟布褂配麻绳腰带。

只提取角色资产图中的视觉设计。严禁生成角色三视图、灰色或白色摄影棚背景、DETAIL SWATCHES 细节格、色卡条、FRONT VIEW / SIDE VIEW / BACK VIEW / TOP-DOWN 等图片原有文字与水印。

【体型比例·必须严格遵守】

全片共有四个身高档位，必须清晰可辨：

第一档（最高）：master，成年男性身高偏高，约 6—7 英尺。他比所有学生都高，是地面上最高的。

第二档（大型）：lion、tiger、polarbear、panda、panther、rhino、cat，约 5—6 英尺。他们的头顶大约到 master 的下巴与肩膀之间，master 略高于他们一头。这一档全部是宽厚壮硕的大体型。

第三档（小型）：redpanda、fennec、koala、rabbit，约 3—4 英尺。他们的身高只有第二档的一半多一点，头顶大约到大型角色的胸口。

第四档（最小）：hamster，约 2—3 英尺，是全场最矮的，比小型档还要明显矮一截，头顶只到小型角色的胸口。

所有角色全程双足直立站立，人形站姿，绝不四足着地、绝不趴伏、绝不蹲坐。全部是拟人化的武术学徒。

fennec 与 redpanda 毛色相近，必须靠轮廓区分：fennec 有一对巨大的、直立向上的尖耳朵，身形纤细；redpanda 耳朵小而圆，身形圆胖，有一条极其蓬松的大尾巴。二者绝不混淆。

【队列站位·必须严格遵守】

11 名学生站成一条横排，面朝镜头，从画面左到右的顺序固定为：

1. rhino（大型）
2. rabbit（小型）
3. tiger（大型）
4. koala（小型）
5. panther（大型）
6. hamster（最小）
7. polarbear（大型）
8. fennec（小型）
9. lion（大型）
10. redpanda（小型）
11. panda（大型）

高矮交错排列，队列的头顶线呈明显的起伏。每个角色在全片中只出现一次，绝不复制、绝不重复出现、绝不多出第 12 名学生。

master 从队列最左端开始，沿着队列向右缓步走过，逐一审视每一张脸。cat 全程不在队列中、不在地面上、不在演武场上——他从第 0 秒起就一直坐在正殿屋顶右侧的檐角上，只是在 28 秒之前不入画。

【场景：clifftemple】

悬崖之巅的古中式寺院。宽阔平整的青灰石板演武场悬于千仞绝壁之上，石板洁净、缝隙间生着青苔；正后方是一座双层瓦顶的木构正殿，殿前有一段宽石阶；两侧有低矮的石栏与几根立柱；崖边生着虬曲的古松；平台三面临深渊，白色云海在崖下缓缓翻涌，远处群峰错落。

【正殿屋顶的结构】正殿有上下两层深蓝灰色的瓦顶。上层屋顶较小，屋脊两端各有一个向上高高翘起的檐角，檐角末端带有走兽状的脊饰；下层屋顶更宽，向四周伸出。整座屋顶的右侧边缘之外就是悬崖，再往外是翻涌的云海、层叠的远山与晨雾。

清晨的高原天光，柔和而清冷，斜斜地从画面左侧射入，在石板上拉出长长的影子。空气中有薄雾与浮尘。

本片中的寺院完整无损，没有战斗痕迹、没有坍塌、没有裂纹。

【刚性空间锚点】正殿及其双层瓦顶、宽石阶、崖边古松、远处群峰的相对位置全片绝对不得漂移、消失或改变数量。

【本片的性质】

这不是打斗场面。全片没有任何战斗、出拳、踢腿、对练或武术动作。这是一场入门集训的第一天点名，全部内容是：走位、审视、表情、五句台词、一次呼喊。

【对白规则】

本片只有五句台词，全部在下方时间码中以引号标出。只有引号内的文字是被说出来的。其余所有文字——包括动作描述、表情描述、运镜说明与语气说明——全部是画面说明，绝对不得念出、不得配音、不得作为旁白。

全片台词不得超过五句。不得出现旁白、不得出现内心独白、不得出现第六句台词。只有 master 说话，11 名学生与 cat 全程一句话都不说。

【运镜规格总纲】

全程一镜到底，绝对禁止硬切、剪辑、黑屏转场与定格。

35mm 电影镜头，稳定的横向轨道跟拍。0—24 秒镜头始终与 master 保持同速平移，从队列左端一路推进到右端，机位高度在 master 的胸口位置。移动平稳、缓慢、有分量，只有极轻微的手持呼吸感。

在每个学生入画时，镜头略微放慢并短暂停顿，让这张脸完整清晰地被看见，随后继续平移。绝不快速掠过、绝不糊掉任何一张脸。

全片没有任何角色完全静止不动——即使站在队列里，也必须有呼吸起伏、毛发在风中轻动、耳朵抽动、尾巴摆动、眼神移动、重心的细微调整。

【第一幕：0—4 秒·集合】

0.0—2.0 秒
广角全景。11 名学生在演武场上站成一条横排，面朝镜头，高矮交错，头顶线明显起伏。晨风掠过，所有人的毛发、耳朵、袍角与尾巴都在轻轻摆动。背后是正殿、崖边古松与翻涌的云海。

master 从画面左侧走入，背对镜头，长发与破损布条在风中飘动。运镜：从高位广角缓缓下降至胸口高度，同时向左横移，跟上 master 的脚步。

2.0—4.0 秒
master 走到队列最左端，在 rhino 面前站定，抬眼看他。rhino 立刻把胸膛挺得更高，下巴抬起，鼻孔喷出一股白气，眼神里全是"我最强"的自信。

master 的语气低沉平缓。
master："从今天起，你们是我的学生。"

运镜：镜头在 rhino 面前短暂停住，随后开始沿队列向右平移。

【第二幕：4—24 秒·逐一审视】

4.0—7.0 秒
master 走过 rabbit。rabbit 全身僵硬，两只长耳朵紧张地贴向后方又弹起来，眼睛瞪得极大，喉咙咽了一下，视线不受控制地瞟向侧面的出口方向——他显然是被吓到了，随时想跑。

紧接着是 tiger。tiger 眼睛发亮，身体不自觉地前倾，尾巴在身后兴奋地左右快速摆动，嘴角忍不住上扬——他是真心想学功夫的那一个。

运镜：持续横移，在两张脸前各短暂放慢。

7.0—10.0 秒
master 走过 koala。koala 眼皮沉重地半垂着，脑袋轻轻往下一点，猛地惊醒，努力睁大眼睛，两秒后眼皮又开始往下掉——他从头到尾都在打瞌睡。

紧接着是 panther。panther 双臂抱在胸前，嘴角挂着一个懒散的坏笑，露出一颗尖牙，眼神斜斜地打量 master，明摆着没把这当回事。

master 的语气不带情绪。
master："这里没有天才，只有肯下苦功的人。"

运镜：持续横移，说话时不停顿。

10.0—13.0 秒
master 走到 hamster 面前——他必须明显低头才能看到这个全场最矮的小家伙。

hamster 站得笔直，两只前爪紧握成拳收在身侧，眉头拧得死紧，仰着头用一双极其严肃、极其凶狠的小眼睛瞪回去。他是全队里最认真的一个，认真到有点好笑。

master 看了他两秒，微微点了一下头，继续往前走。

运镜：镜头随 master 的视线短暂下降到 hamster 的高度，随后升回胸口高度继续横移。

13.0—17.0 秒
master 走过 polarbear。polarbear 一动不动，神情平静沉稳，深色的眼睛安静地回望，看不出任何情绪——他是唯一一个让人猜不透的。

紧接着是 fennec。fennec 那对巨大的耳朵不停地转动、捕捉着四面八方的声音，眼睛好奇地四处打量演武场、正殿与云海，紧张与兴奋同时写在脸上。

master 的语气平淡。
master："我不管你们为什么来。"

运镜：持续横移。

17.0—21.0 秒
master 走过 lion。lion 撇着嘴，肩膀垮着，蓬松的鬃毛遮住半张脸，眼神明显不情愿地飘向别处——他是被家里硬送来的，一百个不乐意。

紧接着是 redpanda。redpanda 双臂交叉抱在胸前，眉头拧成一团，蓬松的大尾巴烦躁地甩来甩去，全身上下都写着"我为什么要在这里"。

运镜：持续横移，在两张脸前各短暂放慢。

21.0—24.0 秒
master 走到队列最右端的 panda 面前。panda 笑得眼睛都眯起来了，热情地朝 master 挥了挥一只毛茸茸的爪子，兴奋得整个身体都在轻轻晃动，完全没有察觉气氛的严肃。

master 停下脚步，转身面向整条队列。

运镜：镜头在 panda 面前停住，随后随 master 的转身缓缓拉开，把整条队列重新纳入画面。

【第三幕：24—30 秒·大弟子】

24.0—26.5 秒
master 站在队列前，目光扫过所有 11 张脸。他的语气第一次带上了一点分量。

master："你们都要给我争气，像我的大弟子一样。"

说完他侧过头，看向队列的一侧，像是要把某个人叫出来展示给大家看。那个位置是空的。

他又看向另一侧。也是空的。

11 名学生的目光全部跟着他转来转去。

运镜：镜头随 master 的视线左右缓缓摇摆，两次都扫过空荡荡的石板地面。
